brief:
The Water Authority confirmed Wednesday that Gaza's sanitation infrastructure faces an unprecedented crisis, with approximately 55,000 cubic meters of untreated sewage discharged daily into the environment, the Shehab Wire reported. The continuous dumping without treatment aggravates environmental and health risks while threatening contamination of the sea and surrounding areas.

The disclosure comes amid severe operational constraints affecting Gaza's waste management capacity. Treatment facilities across the territory have been unable to process incoming sewage flows, forcing authorities to release raw wastewater into coastal and inland zones. Officials have warned that the unchecked discharge poses immediate risks to public health, marine ecosystems, and freshwater resources in the densely populated enclave.
